profile.headline: Software Engineer utilizing laboratory research expertise to develop innovative solutions.
profile.summary:
I'm a dedicated scientific software engineer with extensive experience in software development within the bioscience sector. At the Allen Institute, I write software for petabyte scale data pipelines and develop cloud-hosted web applications.

My research background involves electrophysiology, transcriptomics, neuron morphology, and nanopore DNA sequencing. I hold a double major in biophysics and biochemistry and a minor in applied mathematics from the University of Washington.

I am passionate about applying my life sciences and software engineering expertise to develop innovative solutions in data and software engineering roles.

positions.title: Software Engineer - Scientific Data & Solutions Engineering
positions.description:
- Develop full stack web applications using Python, Javascript, and PostgreSQL on AWS
- Modernize legacy ETL pipelines using TDD, delivering scientific data to GraphQL APIs
- Design and build tool to migrate petabytes of data from on-prem to cloud object store
- Manage and publish datasets, using SLURM, to achieve 10x speedup via parallelism 
- Configure CI/CD pipelines for production software using Docker on GitHub Actions
- Mentor interns and junior engineers on software development best practices
- Act as scrum master, managing agile project timelines across teams in Jira
- Lead winning AI-focused hackathon team, detecting healthy cells using computer vision

positions.title: Research Associate - In Vitro Single Cell Electrophysiology
positions.description:
- Execute triple modality patch-seq experiments on mouse and human neurons, obtaining high quality electrophysiological, transcriptomic, and morphological data
- Write data visualization and analysis software to generate figures for publications
- Identify data quality issues and propose solutions to increase experiment fidelity
- Write and edit standard operating procedures for experimental protocols

positions.title: Laboratory Technician - Nanopore DNA Sequencing & Single Molecule Enzyme Kinetics
positions.description:
- Perform nanopore DNA sequencing and single molecule enzyme kinetics experiments
- Prototype and manufacture custom nanopore experiment devices using machine shop
- Develop and execute cleaning protocols to decontaminate experiments

honors.title: Boas Scholarship
honors.description: The Mary L. Boas Endowed Scholarship recognizes undergraduate women students in the Department of Physics for outstanding academic achievements.
honors.issuer: Issued by UW Physics Department · May 2017

volunteerExperiences.role: Disability Resource Center Note Taker for Physics and Genetics Classes
